Method.summary: Offsets are read out of the client's own reflection database rather than matched against recorded values. Each class descriptor names its properties; each property descriptor points at an accessor record; the getter in that record carries the member offset as an immediate.

routes.reflection harvest: ClassDescriptors are enumerated statically from the module by vtable identity (not via live instances, which capped coverage at whatever the scene contained). Each property descriptor is 0xa0 bytes: +0x08 name, +0x30 the DECLARING class, +0x68 the value type, +0x90 the accessor record {vtable, getter, setter, 0}.
routes.getter decoding: Two decoders. A strict one accounts for a function byte by byte and refuses anything it cannot; a scanning one takes the displacement a getter reads and its setter writes, and is re-validated every run against every property the strict decoder already answered -- a single contradiction disables it.
routes.subobject constant: A getter's `this` is the declaring class's <Class>Prop base, not the Instance, so one constant per (concrete class, declaring class) converts it. Three independent sources: offsets derived structurally, the `lea r,[rcx-D]` adjustment the compiler leaves in thunks, and RTTIBaseClassDescriptor::PMD.mdisp. Published where two agree; RTTI may stand alone, having matched an independent route on every pair where one existed.

checks every value passes: the declaring class's constant is corroborated, not assumed
every concrete class the member is reached through gives one answer
nothing contradicts an offset derived structurally from a live client
no two fields of one class share an offset

known limits.unreadable code: Hyperion decrypts .text on demand and re-protects it. Roughly half of all accessor getters sit on committed PAGE_NOACCESS pages; a read-only tool cannot see them, and they are reported as such rather than counted as decoder gaps.
known limits.not everything is a property: Engine internals -- MaterialColors, task scheduler and renderer fields, Instance.This -- have no property descriptor at all and are out of this mechanism's reach entirely.
known limits.absent, never zero: A field that could not be derived is omitted. A missing offset is a compile error at the use site; a zero is a wrong click.

Note: Every value here was DERIVED from a live client and is accompanied by its evidence. A field that could not be derived is ABSENT, never zero-filled: a number nobody can check is worse than a visible gap.
